chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Manṣūr, from Faḍl al-Aʿwar, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:

We were, at the time of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), when he passed away, wavering like sheep that have no shepherd. Then we met Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, and he said to me, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, who is your Imam?” So I said, “My Imams are the family of Muḥammad.” He said, “You are ruined and have ruined others. Did not you and I hear Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: ‘Whoever dies while there is no Imam over him dies a death of Jāhiliyyah’?” So I said, “Yes, by my life.”

And three days before that, or about that, I had gone in to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and Allah granted recognition. So I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “Indeed Sālim said to me such and such.” He said: So he said, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, no one from among us dies until he leaves behind, after him, one who acts with the like of his deeds, follows his path, and calls to what he called to.”

O Abū ʿUbaydah, what was given to Dāwūd was not withheld from being given to Sulaymān. Then he said, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, when the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) rises, he will judge with the judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān, not asking for evidence.”

key_terms.إِمَامُكَ: your divinely designated Imam whose authority must be recognized
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةَ: recognition and true knowledge of the Imam
key_terms.بَيِّنَةً: formal outward proof or evidentiary testimony
key_terms.بِحُكْمِ دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ: with the mode of judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān through divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.سِيرَتِهِ: his way, conduct, and mode of guidance
key_terms.قَائِمُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the rising Imam from the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: a death resembling the state of pre-Islamic ignorance due to lacking recognition of the Imam
key_terms.يُخَلِّفَ: to leave behind a successor after oneself

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith prove continuous Imamate after the death of an Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the confusion after the passing of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) and affirms that the earth is never left without a rightful Imam from Ahl al-Bayt. It also states that each Imam is succeeded by one who continues his mission, and it points to the Qāʾim of آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ (صلى الله عليه وآله) who will judge with divinely granted knowledge like Dāwūd and Sulaymān.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour, from Fazl Al Awry, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,

‘We were in the time period when Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> passed away. We were wavering like the sheep with no shepherd for them. So we met Salim Bin Abu Hafsa, and he said to me, ‘O Abu Ubeyda! Who is your Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I said, ‘My Imams<sup>asws</sup> are the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’. So he said, ‘You are destroyed and will cause others to be destroyed. Did I and you not hear Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who dies and there isn’t an Imam<sup>asws</sup> over him, died the death of the Pre-Islamic period?’ So I said, ‘Yes, by my life’.

And that had been three days before I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Graced me with the recognition. So I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Salim said to me, such and such’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Ubeyda! It is such that he<sup>asws</sup> does not die from us<sup>asws</sup>, and dying one, until there replaces him<sup>asws</sup> from after him<sup>asws</sup>, the one<sup>asws</sup> who does similar to his<sup>asws</sup> deeds, and by a way of his<sup>asws</sup> ways, and calls to what he<sup>asws</sup> used to call to.

O Abu Ubeyda! It was not prevented, what was Given to Dawood<sup>as</sup> that it be Given to Suleyman<sup>as</sup>’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the Qaim<sup>asws</sup> of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> rises, he<sup>asws</sup> would judge by the judgment of Dawood<sup>as</sup> and Suleyman<sup>asws</sup>, not asking for proof’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu’Umayr from Mansur from al-Fadl al-A ‘al-A ‘war from abu ‘ubayda al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following.

“We lived during the times of abu Ja‘far (a.s.). When he passed away we were left like sheep without shepherd. We met Salim ibn abu Hafs and he said to me, “O abu ‘Ubayda, who is your Imam?” I said, “My Imams are A’l (family) of Muhammad (s.a).” He said, “Did not I and you hear abu Ja‘far (a.s.) say, “Whoever would die without an Imam above him he has died as the death of the age ignorance.” I said, “Yes, that is very true. I can swear by my own life.”

It was only about three days before my meeting with abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) in which meeting Allah granted to me the blessing of recognizing him as my Imam. I said to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) that Salim said to me so and so.” The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) said, “O abu ‘Ubayda, no one of us passes away before appointing a successor that would act and behave just as the preceding Imam and call people to what the Imam before him did.

O abu ‘Ubayda what was given to David did not bar Sulayman from receiving (Allah’s blessings).” Then he said, “O abu ‘Ubayda, when Al-Qa’im (the one who will rise with Divine Authority) will rise he will judge among people the way David and Sulayman had been judging among people. He will call any witness to testify in a case.”
